name: math_tensor_forming

phase_0.boundary_condition: the universal property of the tensor product

VINIT.justification: the zero vector space before any basis vectors are defined

TANCH.justification: the final closed algebraic structure containing all multilinear relations

AFWD.justification: the unique linear transformation from the tensor product to another space

AREV.justification: the contravariant mapping from the product back to the constituent functional forms

CLINK.justification: the sequential application of maps within the category of vector spaces

IMSCRIB.justification: the map that sends every tensor to itself preserving the structure

FSPLIT.justification: the separation of a single bilinear operation into two distinct vector space inputs V and W

FFUSE.justification: the unification of two vector spaces into a single space V ⊗ W

EVALT.justification: the confirmation that the basis vectors satisfy the required independence

EVALF.justification: the failure of the basis to span the space uniquely

ENGAGR.justification: the simultaneous existence of multiple basis representations before measurement

IFIX.justification: the permanent assignment of the rank and dimension to the resulting space

phase_3.void_description: unallocated scalar field without vector structure
phase_3.true_description: valid linear transformation satisfying the universal property
phase_3.false_description: invalid mapping failing to preserve bilinearity
phase_3.both_description: entangled state where multiple basis choices coexist

steps.domain_action: initialize the scalar field and empty basis sets
identify the base vector spaces V and W as distinct entities
branch the operation into the two constituent vector spaces
verify the basis of the first vector space V
map the first basis to the intermediate product state
record the dimension of the first vector space
check for linear dependence in the second vector space W
perform a parity flip to resolve basis orientation in W
record the dimension of the second vector space
combine the two spaces into the tensor product V ⊗ W
compose the bilinear map with the canonical linear map
hold the resulting tensor in a state of basis-independent representation
fix the final rank of the tensor product space
seal the tensor product space within its universal boundary

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the category theory framework defining morphisms and objects
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: the bilinear map acting as the interface between spaces
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the basis set coefficients stored in the coordinate representation
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the order of operations defined by the construction of the free vector space
phase_5.alfs_store: the CLINK L8 Organism reference catalog

phase_6.cycle_cost: computational overhead of calculating the Kronecker product
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: two independent vector spaces of dimension n and m
phase_6.post_cycle_state: one unified vector space of dimension n times m
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the information content is conserved through the universal property
